headline: FOMC HIKES 25 BPS TO 4.00% — GOLD RALLIES $83 POST-DECISION TO $4,389 AS PRICED-IN HIKE TRIGGERS 'BUY THE NEWS'
snippet: The Federal Reserve delivered its first rate hike since 2023, raising the federal funds rate to 4.00% on September 16 as market-implied odds sat near 86–90% certainty; gold initially at $4,306 pre-decision surged to $4,389 (+1.7%) and silver reached $64.98 (+2%) as the well-priced hike triggered classic 'buy the news' positioning — a pattern documented in every previous well-anticipated tightening move since 2015. With the forward guidance read as neutral rather than hawkish, Goldman Sachs' $4,900 and JPMorgan's $4,500 year-end targets remain unchanged and the primary near-term headwind for precious metals has now cleared.

headline: WHEATON'S INVESTOR DAY MAPS $4.3B ANTAMINA STREAM — RECORD H1 $1.8B REVENUE AS LARGEST STREAMING DEAL EVER RESETS GROWTH STORY
snippet: Wheaton Precious Metals (NYSE/TSX: WPM) hosted its September 16 Investor Day, presenting the strategic context behind the $4.3B Antamina silver stream with BHP (the largest precious metals streaming transaction ever, closed April 1, 2026) alongside record H1 2026 results of $1.8B revenue, $1.1B net earnings, and $1.4B operating cash flow. New streams added in 2026 include Jervois in Australia and Spanish Mountain and Cipango in Canada, with management outlining how the Antamina production profile reshapes Wheaton's growth curve through 2035.

headline: POWER METALLIC MAIDEN LION ZONE RESOURCE: 4.75MT AT 3.9% CUEQ — 98%+ COPPER RECOVERY IN LOCKED-CYCLE TESTS, 5 RIGS TURNING IN QUEBEC
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSXV: PNPN) released a maiden NI 43-101 resource for the Lion Zone at its Nisk project in Quebec — 4.75 million tonnes averaging approximately 3.9% copper equivalent incorporating copper, palladium, platinum, gold, silver, and nickel, with more than 85% classified in the Indicated category. SGS Canada locked-cycle metallurgical tests returned over 98% copper recovery and concentrate grades above 25% Cu. Five rigs are active at the project and a Preliminary Economic Assessment is being commissioned to advance Nisk toward prefeasibility.

headline: CENTRAL ASIA METALS LOCKS IN CYGNUS VOTE FOR SEPT 18 — KAZAKHSTAN ANTITRUST DUE OCT 1 IN A$232M COPPER-GOLD GRAB
snippet: Central Asia Metals PLC (LSE: CAML) provided a September 14 scheme update confirming the Cygnus Metals (ASX: CY5) shareholder meeting for September 18 in Perth, with the Kazakhstan regulatory approval condition precedent requiring resolution by October 1 and deal effective date targeted September 24 with implementation October 5. The all-share transaction valued at A$232 million adds the Chibougamau copper-gold project in Quebec and the Berta zinc project to CAML's existing Kazakhstan and North Macedonia portfolio, accelerating the company's critical minerals diversification into stable mining jurisdictions.

headline: ROYAL ROAD DRILLS AT GÜÍNTAR, COLOMBIA — 36M AT 2.14 G/T GOLD IN ROCK-CHIP AS NEW HOLES TARGET DEPTH BELOW HISTORIC 176M INTERCEPT
snippet: Royal Road Minerals (TSXV: RYR) announced September 14 that diamond drilling has commenced at Güíntar, its most advanced gold-copper-silver target in Antioquia, Colombia, with multiple drill platforms testing down-plunge extensions below the historic 176 metres at 1.2 g/t AuEq intercept. Recent underground rock-chip sampling at the nearby Algodona prospect returned 36 metres averaging 2.14 g/t Au and 6.95 g/t Ag, confirming a broader multi-target system across the company's Colombian land package; assay results from the current program are expected in Q4 2026.

headline: VOLTA DRILLS 214M OF RARE EARTHS AND GALLIUM IN ONTARIO — SPRINGER HITS 0.8% TREO PLUS 63.8 G/T GALLIUM IN BREAKTHROUGH COMBO
snippet: Volta Metals reported that drill hole SL26-28 at the Springer project in northern Ontario intersected 214.5 metres grading 0.8% total rare earth oxides alongside 63.8 grams of gallium per tonne — a significant domestic combination of light rare earths and a semiconductor-critical metal subject to China's ongoing export restrictions. The intersection differentiates Springer sharply from typical Canadian rare earth plays; gallium is a key input for III-V semiconductors, solar cells, and defence electronics, and Western ex-China supply remains deeply constrained following China's 2023 gallium export controls.

headline: $54B ANGLO-TECK MERGER ENTERS CHINA DECISION WINDOW — BEIJING ANTITRUST REVIEW OPEN; CLOSE TARGETED BY MARCH 2027
snippet: Anglo American and Teck Resources' proposed $54B merger of equals — which would create the world's fifth-largest copper producer at 1.2 million tonnes per year — has entered its China Anti-Monopoly Law review window for September 2026 through March 2027, with South Korea the only other pending jurisdiction. CEO Duncan Wanblad has confirmed active engagement with Chinese regulators; the transaction received overwhelming shareholder approval in December 2025 and Canadian Investment Canada Act clearance in early 2026, with a combined entity that would hold Quebrada Blanca, Carmen de Andacollo, and Highland Valley Copper among its assets.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM MINERS UP 17% IN SEPTEMBER, JUNIOR INDEX +21.75% — CONVICTION BUYING PERSISTS AS SPOT HOLDS $90/LB
snippet: Sprott's September uranium market update documents miners significantly outpacing bullion this month — the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index gained 17.01% and junior uranium miners advanced 21.75% as spot uranium held near $90/lb. Supply risks have deepened following Cameco's McArthur River production guidance reduction and Kazatomprom's 8-million-pound quota cut for 2026, leaving U.S. utilities with approximately 52% of 2026–2035 requirements uncontracted; the long-term contract price topping $96.50/lb for the first time since 2007 has accelerated utility re-engagement in term procurement.

headline: 55 DAYS TO NOVEMBER 10: CHINA'S RARE EARTH CONTROLS CLOCK TICKS — FASTMARKETS: WESTERN REFINING STILL YEARS AWAY FROM SELF-SUFFICIENCY
snippet: Fastmarkets analysis examines Western preparedness as China's November 10, 2026 deadline for reimplementation of rare earth export controls approaches — the suspension of the October 2025 expanded controls expires in 55 days, covering holmium, erbium, thulium, europium, and ytterbium, added to existing licence requirements on samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium. Western refining and recycling capacity remains years from self-sufficiency for the affected elements; the analysis profiles non-Chinese developers including Energy Fuels, MP Materials, and Vital Metals that would receive structural demand tailwinds under reimplementation.

headline: GOLD MINERS VS. BULLION POST-FOMC: THE LEVERAGE MATH AS HIKE CLEARS — 3.5X OPERATING LEVERAGE SHOULD CLOSE THE 41-QUARTER DISCOUNT
snippet: With the Fed hike now fully in the rear-view mirror, GoldSilver.com's post-FOMC analysis argues that the primary near-term headwind for gold equities has cleared: at $4,300+ gold, the sector's historical 3.5x operating leverage should produce outsized miner equity returns relative to bullion, yet GDXJ constituents still trade at a 41-quarter valuation trough near 16x trailing P/E despite record Q2 2026 cash flows of $17.2B across the GDX top 25. The piece frames this as the most structurally compelling gold equity entry since 2016, with the post-hike removal of rate uncertainty the catalyst the sector has been waiting for.
